section.sectionSummaryBrief: Through repentance out of love, the past is transformed, enabling all one's years to be equal for good, and this explains the connection between the two interpretations of Sarah's life.
section.t: And one can explain the elucidation of this,
that through repentance out of love, even the past is changed,
and therefore it is within the power of each person
(even one who sinned and blemished and transgressed the path)
that all his years
(even his years of the past)
should be equal for good.
And based on this, one can explain the connection and relevance of the two interpretations of “the years of the life of Sarah,”
that “all of them were equally good,”
for all matters in physicality descend from their counterpart in spirituality,
and through the matter of “all of them were life” regarding supernal life,
thereby it is brought about that “all of them were life” also regarding life in its simple sense,
that the life is hers and she becomes the master over them,
and through this, power is given to every Jew
that all the years of his life
(even the years that have passed)
should be his and that he should be the master over them,
and therefore it is in his power that all his years
(even the years of the past)
should be equal for good.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Every Jew can be a Beinoni at any time through free will to fulfill the mitzvah of repentance, which reveals the innate repentance within, making past transgressions as if they never occurred.
section.t: And based on this, one can understand what is written in Tanya,
that every person can be a Beinoni at any time and any hour,
for at first glance,
since a Beinoni is one who never committed a transgression in his life and was never called wicked even for one hour or one moment all his days,
how can every person
(including even one who committed a transgression)
be a Beinoni?
And one can explain the elucidation of this,
that just as regarding all the mitzvos, permission is given to every person and there is none who can prevent him,
so too is it regarding the mitzvah of repentance,
that every Jew has free choice to fulfill the mitzvah of repentance.
And one can say,
that the choice regarding the mitzvah of repentance is even greater than regarding other mitzvos.
Because repentance is a general mitzvah,
and therefore there is a special empowerment given for it.
And also,
since every Jew wants to fulfill all the mitzvos and distance himself from transgressions, only his evil inclination overpowered him,
so when he committed a transgression, contrary to the will of his true self,
in his innermost being he regrets and is distressed and worried about it.
That is,
that in his innermost being he repents
immediately.
And therefore, that there is none who can prevent him from fulfilling the mitzvah of repentance is
(in a particular sense)
greater than regarding other mitzvos,
for in order to fulfill this mitzvah, he does not need a new action or deed, only to reveal the repentance that is in his innermost being.
And this is that every person can be a Beinoni at any time and any hour,
for since he has free choice to fulfill the mitzvah of repentance,
and the essence and perfection of repentance is repentance out of love,
through which his transgression is uprooted from its very beginning,
so it is within his ability to be a Beinoni who never committed a transgression in his life.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Each interpretation of Sarah's life includes the other, as the concept of all being equal for good contains the idea of life being hers, and vice versa.
section.t: And one may add in explaining the connection and relevance of the two interpretations of “the years of the life of Sarah,”
that “all of them were life” and “all of them were equal,”
that in each of them both matters are included.
For also in the interpretation that “the years of the life of Sarah” means they were all equally good,
the matter of “all of them were life” is included
[as above in section 2,
that in order for all to be equally good, even the years of the past,
it is through that the years of his life are his],
and likewise conversely,
that also in the interpretation that “the years of the life of Sarah” means “all of them were life,”
the matter of “all of them were equal” is included.
